convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in MT5 indicators (iMA, iCCI, iStochastic). Simple entry/exit rules with fixed or percentage-based position sizing. External .mqh includes (Trade.mqh, SymbolInfo.mqh, DealInfo.mqh, PositionInfo.mqh) are standard MT5 trading library helpers, not custom trading logic.

derived_values.name: ma_shift: effective MA bar shift
derived_values.used_by: MA indicator buffer copy and signal comparison

derived_values.name: p_shift: effective price bar shift
derived_values.used_by: Close price copy for signal comparison

derived_values.name: ZeroBar: whether any effective shift equals zero
derived_values.used_by: New bar guard logic - if true, signals evaluated every tick on bar 0

long.left: CCI < -CCIDiffer AND Stochastic Main < 50-StDiffer AND Close > MA

short.left: CCI > CCIDiffer AND Stochastic Main > 50+StDiffer AND Close < MA

other_exits: MWMode: if enabled, SL/TP are set after position open via PositionModify to handle brokers that reject SL/TP with order; SL/TP temporarily stored in global variables then applied post-open

position_sizing.conditional_logic: If Lots input > 0, use fixed lot size; if Lots == 0, calculate as AccountFreeMargin * MaximumRisk / 1000.0, then normalize to symbol volume step/min/max constraints

custom_logic_notes: MWMode (Modify-After-Open): When enabled, the EA opens positions with SL=0 and TP=0, stores intended SL/TP in global variables, then modifies the position on subsequent ticks to set actual SL/TP. This works around brokers that reject stop levels at order time. New bar guard has exception: if ZeroBar is true (any effective shift is 0), signals are evaluated every tick on bar 0 instead of once per bar. Deviation is set dynamically to Spread*3 for each trade. Close uses spread-based deviation via Trade.PositionClose with Spread*3 timeout. Entry also checks that opposite close signal is not active (e.g. OpenBuy && !OpenSell && !CloseBuy).
python_conversion_notes: Straightforward conversion. All three indicators (MA, CCI, Stochastic) are standard and available in most Python charting/TA libraries (ta-lib, pandas-ta). Signal logic is simple AND conditions comparing indicator values to thresholds. MWMode is a broker-workaround that can be simplified in Python since backtesting frameworks don't have broker rejection issues. Position sizing conditional logic (fixed vs risk-based) needs branching. The CommonShift parameter is added to all indicator shifts, defaulting to bar [1] lookback (shift=1) which means signals are based on confirmed bar data - safe for backtesting. The ZeroBar edge case should be noted but is unlikely in production use with CommonShift=1. No digit adjustment needed - SL/TP are in points directly via Sym.Point().
